name: Build
question: Does every checkpoint pass its checks, smallest first?
do: Check the starting point first: it builds and every existing check is green.
Per checkpoint: write its checks and see them fail; a worker makes them pass; the Mechanical gate runs every check a machine can run; the Review gate sends a fresh checker after what the checks miss.
A stop hook keeps the work going while a gate is open (later; today the orchestrator holds the gate). A counterexample to a claim, or three rounds without passing, go back to Specify.
When every checkpoint has passed: Gate B. You try it as a person would; your feedback becomes new checkpoints through the same gates.
Then it is released, with an undo that was tested (later automatic; today you or the orchestrator publish by hand).
output: every checkpoint through both gates · your try · release · tested undo
gate_text: Gate B: you tried it. Release follows by itself.
who: The orchestrator, worker and checker agents in fresh contexts, machines; you at Gate B.
from: Claude Code team: verifier, reviewer, stopping rules, undo
Shopify Helix: checkpoints, enforced gates, critic and fixer
